findings.message: An open item whose marker has no `class:`, or has a class outside CLASSES, is treated as `other` and never blocks. This happens even when the line's own label says blocker or major, for example lines written by a pre-0.9.7 specclaw-review or edited by hand. The review side fails closed on unlabelled blockers and majors (`unclassified`), so the two sides disagree. Fix: when the marker is missing or its class is unknown, read the severity from the leading `[... blocker|major ...]` label and treat the item as `unclassified`.
findings.scenario: follow-ups.md at target adds `- [major B8] \`a.py:1\` token logged (round 3) <!-- fp:abc -->` (no class) -> `specclaw-sync release base target` exits 0 and the item is listed as `other`.

findings.message: `git()` decodes with `text=True`. A debt.md, follow-ups.md or config.yaml blob, or a path, that is not valid UTF-8 raises UnicodeDecodeError outside the GateError handler. Python then prints a traceback and exits 1, which is the 'blocking items' code, instead of 2 ('unreadable list'). A read failure is reported as a gate verdict. Fix: decode with errors='surrogateescape', or catch UnicodeDecodeError and exit 2.

The docs say branch policy 'can require' `specclaw/review-loop`, but they do not say that an AzDO PR status stays satisfied across later pushes unless the policy has 'Reset status whenever there are new changes' turned on. The azdo-pr comment mentions this. The SKILL and ci/azure-pipelines.yml header do not. Document that the reset condition is required.

The comment says that when the host has not caught up with the bookkeeping push, the gate 'posts nothing'. In fact the older head is usually the round-records commit, which `verdict --head` accepts, so the status is posted on that older SHA and not on the final head. The same comment appears in specclaw-azdo-pr. Correct the comment so it matches the behaviour.
